issue.title: apply_patch AX: delete patches silently truncate, success message is not evidence, and path/format errors misdescribe the rule
issue.body:
### What happened?

I ran a structured agent-experience evaluation of the `apply_patch` tool: built a fixture package (TS, JS, JSON, Markdown) and drove ~15 patches through the tool using only the tool description as guidance, recording every failure and every point of hesitation, then read `packages/tools/src/tools/apply-patch.ts` to root-cause each one.

The core mechanics are sound. What is not sound is the **feedback**: several failures report a symptom rather than the cause, one error actively instructs you to do the wrong thing, and one operation reports success while doing something different from what was asked. That last one is very likely the mechanism behind #2133 ("the apply_patch output says it succeeded, but the changes aren't in the file"), which was closed without a root cause.

Fixtures and reproductions are in `tmp/applypatchtest/` on a scratch branch; every case below was actually executed, not reasoned about.

### What did you expect to happen?

Errors that name the cause and the remedy, and a success message that is evidence the intended change landed where intended.

---

## Bugs

**B1. A delete patch reports success but leaves a 0-byte file.**

    --- a/deprecated.ts
    +++ /dev/null
    @@ -1,3 +0,0 @@
    -export function oldHelper(): string {
    -  return 'this file exists only to be deleted by a patch';
    -}

Result: `Successfully applied patch to file: .../src/deprecated.ts.` The file still exists, truncated to zero bytes.

This is not "deletion is unsupported" — `validatePatchTarget` has an explicit `isDeleteToNull` branch that deliberately accepts these patches, and `classifyPatchOperations` computes a rename/delete classification. But `writeAndFormatResult` unconditionally calls `writeTextFile`, there is no `unlink` anywhere in the file, and the classification result is consumed only by the LSP diagnostics helper. So the tool advertises the capability, accepts the patch, reports success, and silently does the wrong thing. There is no test for the delete case (the `/dev/null` test at `apply-patch.test.ts:154` covers creation only).

**B2. Doubled error prefix.** A context failure returns:

    Failed to apply patch: Failed to apply patch: context mismatch

`applyPatch` throws `new Error('Failed to apply patch: context mismatch')` and the catch re-applies the same prefix.

**B3. Patching a file that does not exist reports "context mismatch".** `readCurrentContent` swallows ENOENT and returns an empty string, so the failure surfaces as a context mismatch rather than "file does not exist". The agent then goes hunting for a stale-context problem that isn't there.

**B4. The schema does not describe the tool's actual requirements.** `required: ['patch_content']` — yet a call without `absolute_path`/`file_path` is rejected by `validateToolParamValues`. A model reading the schema concludes the path is optional. (Same defect class as #3019, just fixed in #3029.)

---

## AX defects: correct behavior, unusable messaging

**A1. The path-mismatch error tells you to do the wrong thing.** This cost me two failed calls on my very first patch.

Patching `<root>/tmp/applypatchtest/src/calculator.ts` with the natural header `--- a/src/calculator.ts` gives:

    Patch header target "src/calculator.ts" does not match absolute_path "calculator.ts".

That implies the expected value is the basename. It is not — `headerMatches` accepts **either** a bare basename **or** the full path relative to the workspace root. I confirmed both: `a/calculator.ts` works and `a/tmp/applypatchtest/src/calculator.ts` works; only the partial `a/src/calculator.ts` fails. The rule is defensible (the code comment explains it prevents a same-named file in another directory from validating), but the message names only `path.basename(filePath)` as the target, so it hides the valid full-relative form and steers you to the one that looks wrong. Consequence: a straight `git diff` of any file in a subdirectory is rejected, and the error does not explain why.

**A2. Headerless and Codex-style patches fail with `"(unknown)"`.** Omitting `---`/`+++` entirely — reasonable, since `absolute_path` already names the file — gives:

    Patch header target "(unknown)" does not match absolute_path "calculator.ts".

The same message appears for a `*** Begin Patch` / `*** Update File:` envelope. Nothing says "a `---`/`+++` header is required" or what format is accepted. Worth weighting: `apply_patch` is the *Codex* tool name, so models will emit the Codex envelope, and the failure message gives them nothing to correct toward.

**A3. Hunk-count mismatches surface a raw jsdiff symptom.** Declaring `@@ -28,6 +28,11 @@` while supplying 8 old lines gives:

    Failed to parse patch: Unknown line 15 "     return this.history;"

The named line is fine; the header count is wrong. This is the error a model is most likely to hit, because the counts are pure bookkeeping arithmetic. Note the asymmetry: **line numbers are ignored** (I applied a hunk labelled `@@ -40,3 +40,4 @@` to content at line 15 and it landed correctly), but **counts are strictly enforced**. So the tolerant part is the part humans get right, and the strict part is the part models get wrong. Credit where due: an under-declared count fails loudly rather than silently dropping the trailing line — I verified a dropped `+` line errors rather than applying partially.

**A4. The success message is not evidence.** It is exactly `Successfully applied patch to file: <path>.` — no hunk count, no line where it landed, no note that the location differed from the stated one. Because matching relocates silently (A5), success does not tell you the change went where you meant. I had to follow **every single patch with a read call** to confirm. That round-trip is the whole AX cost of this tool, and it is also the reported symptom in #2133: the model saw success, believed it, and only later discovered the file was not what it expected.

**A5. Ambiguous context resolves silently to the nearest match.** With two identical blocks in one file and a deliberately wrong line hint of 87, the patch applied to the *second* block with no warning. Nearest-match is a reasonable strategy, but it is unannounced, and combined with A4 it means a wrong line number can silently edit the wrong occurrence. Note the sibling `replace` tool takes the opposite stance and *rejects* ambiguous matches ("if old_string appears more than once the edit is rejected"). Two editing tools in the same codebase disagreeing on ambiguity is itself a hazard.

---

## Documentation gap

The entire tool description is:

> Applies a unified diff format patch to a file. This tool parses the patch content and applies it to the target file. The patch_content parameter should contain a valid unified diff patch. The tool will parse, validate, and apply the patch, returning the result.

It documents none of the rules a caller must actually satisfy: single file per call; `---`/`+++` header mandatory; header path must be basename or workspace-relative; `/dev/null` creation supported; line numbers tolerant but counts strict; Codex envelope unsupported. Every one of these I had to discover by failing.

---

## What works well (so it does not get broken)

- Multi-hunk patches in one call.
- Line-number tolerance — genuinely good design, do not "fix" this.
- Trailing-newline handling: `\ No newline at end of file` round-trips correctly, verified by hexdump.
- A truly empty line used as blank context (instead of a single space) is tolerated — a very common model error.
- Full `git diff` output with `diff --git` and `index` lines is accepted.
- `/dev/null` → file creation works.
- **The multi-file rejection message is the model the others should follow:** "apply_patch accepts a single target file patch, but the patch_content contained 2 file sections. Use a separate apply_patch call per file." It states the constraint and the remedy in one line. Every message flagged above could be brought to this standard.

---

## Suggested fixes, in priority order

1. Implement delete for `+++ /dev/null` (unlink, and report deletion), or reject delete patches explicitly. Add coverage — the current behavior is a silent data-shape bug. (B1)
2. Report where the patch landed: hunks applied, target line, and an explicit note when the applied position differs from the stated one, or when the context matched in more than one place. This closes the verification round-trip and addresses the #2133 symptom directly. (A4, A5)
3. Rewrite the path-mismatch error to state both accepted forms and show the workspace-relative path for the given `absolute_path`. (A1)
4. Detect a missing/unrecognized header and say so, naming the expected format, instead of `"(unknown)"`. Consider simply accepting a headerless patch, since `absolute_path` already identifies the file. (A2)
5. Translate the jsdiff count error into "hunk header declares N old / M new lines but the body contains X / Y". (A3)
6. Distinguish ENOENT from context mismatch. (B3)
7. Fix the doubled prefix. (B2)
8. Add `absolute_path`/`file_path` to the schema's stated requirements, or make the schema express the either/or. (B4)
9. Expand the tool description to state the rules above.

### Client information

0.11.0-nightly, branch at 75a5cb5d95

### Anything else we need to know?

Related: #2133 (closed, same symptom, no root cause). The evaluation was done first-contact — description only, no source reading — precisely so the discovery cost was measurable; source was consulted afterwards only to root-cause each failure.

expected: The delete patch removes src/deprecated.ts (or the tool reports that deletion is unsupported), and the success message reflects what actually happened.
defect: apply_patch reports "Successfully applied patch to file: .../src/deprecated.ts." but the file still exists, truncated to 0 bytes.

fault location.explanation: Explicitly accepts `+++ /dev/null` delete patches (isDeleteToNull), advertising deletion support; PR #3060 keeps the acceptance but carries the delete classification through to execution.
Computes classifyPatchOperations() but only forwards it for LSP diagnostics; the applied (empty) content is always written back; PR #3060 branches on the delete operation.

Unconditionally calls writeTextFile(filePath, newContent) (no unlink anywhere) and then reports 'Successfully applied patch'; PR #3060 deletes the file for delete patches and makes the success message describe the verified outcome.

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/vybestack/llxprt-code/pull/3060. In v0.10.0, apply_patch validates the patch header, and validatePatchTarget deliberately accepts delete-style patches whose new header is /dev/null. execute then applies the hunk with Diff.applyPatch, which for a full-file removal yields an empty string, and writeAndFormatResult always writes that content back with writeTextFile and returns 'Successfully applied patch to file'. classifyPatchOperations does recognise the delete, but its result is only passed to the LSP diagnostics helper, and the file has no unlink path, so the file remains as a 0-byte file under a success message. Commit 98e6e0e (PR #3060, 'Make apply_patch feedback truthful: deletes delete, success is evidence, errors name the cause') adds a delete branch that removes the file, verifies the result before reporting success, and also fixes the doubled 'Failed to apply patch:' prefix (line 435 plus the catch at 441-444) and the ENOENT-as-context-mismatch message. The fix first ships in v0.11.0, the pinned version, so the case is tested at v0.10.0.
